items.stem: How many square centimetres are there in 1 square metre?
Explain why 1 m² is not equal to 100 cm².
items.answer: 1 m² is a square 100 cm by 100 cm, so its area is 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm².
items.markingKey: B1 uses 1 m = 100 cm for both dimensions; B1 conclusion 10 000 cm² [2]

items.stem: Explain why the conversion factor from m³ to cm³ is 1 000 000 and not 100.
items.answer: A cube of side 1 m is 100 cm × 100 cm × 100 cm = 1 000 000 cm³: the length factor 100 is cubed for volume.
items.markingKey: B1 three dimensions each × 100; B1 100³ = 1 000 000 [2]

items.stem: Mohammed has a fish tank in the shape of a cuboid measuring 50 cm by 20 cm by 35 cm. Calculate the capacity of the tank in litres.
A water trough in a farm near Doha is a cuboid 0.8 m long, 0.9 m wide and 1.25 m deep. Calculate its capacity in litres.

An ornamental pond in a park in Nairobi is a cuboid 4 m long, 2 m wide and 0.75 m deep. (a) Write down the capacity in litres. (b) Water flows in at 500 litres per minute. Calculate the time taken to fill it from empty, in hours and minutes (to the nearest minute).
items.markingKey: (a) B1 × 1000 = 6000 litres [1] (b) M1 6000 ÷ 500 = 12 minutes; M1 ÷ 60 for hours; A1 12 min [3]

items.stem: How many cubic centimetres are there in 1 litre?
items.markingKey: 1 litre = 1000 ml = 1000 cm³.

items.stem: Explain why the same area has a larger number when measured in mm² than when measured in cm².
items.answer: Each cm² contains 10 × 10 = 100 mm², so the number of (smaller) units needed is 100 times larger.
items.markingKey: B1 1 cm² = 100 mm²; B1 smaller unit so more of them [2]

items.stem: A carton is labelled 1.5 litres. Explain how you know its capacity is 1500 cm³.
Isla converts 2.25 m³ to litres by multiplying by 100 and gets 225 litres. Explain the mistake and give the correct answer.
items.answer: Isla used a length (or wrong) factor; 1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³ = 1000 litres, so the answer is 2250 litres.
items.markingKey: B1 identifies the wrong conversion factor (1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³ = 1000 litres); B1 correct answer 2250 litres [2]

items.stem: A rectangular bathroom wall measures 4.25 m by 1.5 m. Calculate its area in cm².
Convert 2.5 m³ to cm³, giving your answer in standard form.
items.markingKey: B1 1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³; B1 2.5 × 10⁶ cm³.

items.stem: A water trough near Nairobi is a cuboid 1.2 m long, 0.6 m wide and 0.8 m deep. Leila fills it to 90% of its depth using a bucket that holds 12 litres. Calculate the least number of full buckets Leila must pour in to reach this level.
items.markingKey: M1 V = 0.576 m³ = 576 litres; M1 × 90% = 518.4 litres; M1 ÷ 12 = 43.2; A1 round up to 44.

items.stem: An ornamental pond in a park in Lisbon is a cuboid 5 m long, 3 m wide and 1 m deep. (a) Write down the capacity in litres. (b) Calculate the area of the base in cm².
A rainwater tank on a school roof in Bangkok is a cuboid 2.5 m by 2 m by 1.2 m high. (a) Calculate the area of the base in cm². (b) Explain why the number of litres is 1000 times the number of m³.
items.answer: (a) 50,000 cm² (b) 1 m³ = 100 × 100 × 100 cm³ = 1 000 000 cm³ and 1 litre = 1000 cm³, so 1 m³ = 1000 litres.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 5 m² × 10 000; A1 50,000 cm² [2] (b) B1 1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³; B1 ÷ 1000 cm³ per litre [2]

items.markingKey: pm times after 1 pm: add 12 to the hours, 4 + 12 = 16.

items.stem: Write 00:20 using the 12-hour clock.
items.markingKey: 00:xx is in the hour after midnight, written 12:xx am

items.stem: Kenji says 2.5 hours is 2 hours 50 minutes. Explain his mistake.
items.answer: 0.5 hours is half of 60 minutes, which is 30 minutes, so 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes.
items.markingKey: B1 0.5 h = 30 min (not 50); B1 2 h 30 min [2]

items.stem: Daniel records that a ferry crossing started at 5:05 pm and finished at 21:20. Calculate how long it lasted, in hours and minutes.

items.stem: Felix takes a train from Ottawa to Toronto. The train leaves at 18:20 and is timetabled to arrive at 20:35. The distance is 216 km. (a) Calculate the timetabled journey time. (b) Calculate the average speed of the train in km/h.
Explain why you cannot find the time from 09:45 to 11:20 by working out 11.20 − 9.45.
items.answer: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so times do not subtract like decimals. The correct duration is 1 h 35 min, not 1.75.
items.markingKey: B1 60 minutes in an hour; B1 correct duration 1 h 35 min [2]

items.stem: Elena wants the length of a journey from 15:45 to 17:15. Elena works out 17.15 − 15.45 = 1.70 and says the journey takes 1 hours 70 minutes. Explain why this is wrong and find the correct time taken.
items.answer: There are 60 minutes, not 100, in an hour, so times cannot be subtracted as decimals. Correct duration: 1 h 30 min.
items.markingKey: B1 explains base 60 not 100; B1 1 h 30 min (e.g. 15:45 → 16:00 is 15 min, then to 17:15) [2]

items.markingKey: B1 any column: 07:50 to 08:53 = 1 h 3 min.

items.markingKey: M1 converts to the same clock (11:15 am = 11:15) and counts on; A1 9 h 55 min.

items.stem: A length is 12 cm to the nearest centimetre. Explain why the upper bound is written as 12.5 cm and not 12.49 cm.
items.answer: Every value up to, but not including, 12.5 rounds to 12, and there is no largest such value below 12.5 (12.49, 12.499, … all round to 12), so 12.5 is used as the boundary.
items.markingKey: B1 values less than 12.5 round to 12; B1 no largest value below 12.5 so 12.5 is the bound [2]

items.stem: Explain why the upper bound of a − b uses the lower bound of b.
items.answer: Subtracting a smaller number leaves a larger result, so the largest difference comes from the largest a and the smallest b.
items.markingKey: B1 largest a; B1 smallest b gives largest difference [2]

items.answer: (a) 1362.75 m² (b) The length and width are rounded, so the area could be anywhere from 1362.75 m² up to (not including) 1437.75 m².
items.markingKey: (a) M1 34.5 × 39.5; A1 1362.75 m² [2] (b) B1 measurements rounded; B1 area lies between bounds [2]

items.stem: The mass of a parcel is d = 6.59 kg, correct to 2 decimal places. Which is the error interval for d?
items.markingKey: Half the rounding unit is 0.005; 6.585 ≤ d < 6.595.

items.stem: Explain why an answer worked out from rounded measurements may not be given to more significant figures than the bounds agree to.
items.answer: The true value could be anywhere between the lower and upper bounds; only the figures that the bounds share are certain.
items.markingKey: B1 true value lies between bounds; B1 only agreed figures are reliable [2]

items.stem: Explain why the error interval for a length of 8 m (nearest metre) is 7.5 ≤ l < 8.5 and not 7.5 ≤ l ≤ 8.5.
items.answer: 8.5 rounds up to 9, so 8.5 itself is not included, but 7.5 rounds up to 8 so it is included.
items.markingKey: B1 8.5 rounds to 9 (strict); B1 7.5 rounds to 8 (included) [2]

items.answer: The largest difference uses the upper bound of a and the lower bound of b: 68.5 − 23.5 = 45 cm.

items.stem: On a conversion graph between two currencies, what does the gradient of the line represent?
items.markingKey: Gradient = change in one currency ÷ change in the other = exchange rate.

items.stem: Explain why the conversion graph from °C to °F does not pass through the origin.
items.answer: 0 °C is 32 °F, not 0 °F, so the two scales are not in direct proportion and the line cuts the °F axis at 32.
items.markingKey: B1 0 °C = 32 °F; B1 not direct proportion / intercept 32 [2]

items.stem: Explain why a value read from a conversion graph is only an estimate.
items.answer: Reading a scale by eye is limited by the size of the squares and the thickness of the line, so the reading is approximate.
items.markingKey: B1 reading by eye/scale; B1 approximate value [2]

items.stem: A school bag costs $75.00 in Madrid and ₹6,739.00 in Bangkok. The exchange rate is 1 US dollar = ₹83.20. Find where it is cheaper and by how much, in US dollars.
items.markingKey: M1 6739 ÷ 83.2 = $81.00; A1 comparison and difference $6.00.

Why does a conversion graph between two currencies pass through the origin?
options: 0 in one currency is worth 0 in the other
Because there is always a commission
items.answer: 0 in one currency is worth 0 in the other
items.markingKey: The currencies are in direct proportion, so (0, 0) lies on the line.

items.stem: A tourist changes money and then immediately changes it back. Explain why they usually get back less than they started with.
items.answer: Banks sell currency at a less favourable rate than they buy it and may also charge commission, so value is lost on each exchange.
items.markingKey: B1 different buy/sell rates; B1 commission/fees [2]

items.stem: Describe how you would use a straight-line conversion graph from kilometres to miles to convert 250 km, if the graph only goes up to 100 km.
items.answer: Read off a value such as 50 km (about 31 miles) and multiply by 5, because the quantities are in direct proportion.
items.markingKey: B1 read a convenient value; B1 scale up using proportion [2]

items.stem: The exchange rate is 1 pound = $1.27. Diego wants to change $1,200.00 into pounds and works out 1200 × 1.27 = 1524. Explain the mistake and find the correct amount.
items.answer: Diego should divide, because each unit of pounds costs 1.27 US dollars: 1200 ÷ 1.27 = £944.88.
items.markingKey: B1 should divide (converting from US dollars to pounds); B1 £944.88 [2]

items.stem: A straight-line conversion graph passes through (0, 0) and (50 miles, 80 km). Use it to convert 20 miles to kilometres.

(a) Calculate how many South African rand Elena receives. (b) At the end of the trip Elena changes the money left back into euros at a rate of 1 euro = R 20.8. Calculate how much Elena receives, to the nearest cent.
